subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw apply before repairing or opening an active session transcript that is large enough to crash the gateway on restart?
rationale: Source proof shows the failure boundary is real, but the safe product behavior depends on a maintainer choice between preserving history, quarantining/skipping dangerous sessions, truncating old entries, or requiring a doctor-mediated recovery.

options.title: Quarantine Then Doctor Recovery
options.body: Move oversized crash-prone active transcripts out of the hot startup/open path by default, mark the session degraded, and provide a doctor or visible recovery flow for inspection and restoration.

options.title: Bounded Tail Load
options.body: Load only a bounded tail or compacted summary for oversized transcripts, accepting more automatic history loss in exchange for fewer manual recovery steps.

options.title: Marker Cap Only
options.body: Land only the bootstrap-entry circuit breaker first, accepting that full-transcript OOM recovery remains open as a separate later decision.

recommendation.title: Quarantine Then Doctor Recovery
recommendation.body: Move oversized crash-prone active transcripts out of the hot startup/open path by default, mark the session degraded, and provide a doctor or visible recovery flow for inspection and restoration.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest recent owner across the active embedded runner, bootstrap, repair, and session manager paths that would carry the policy.
